_readme: Pairs of pages that deliberately offer the same typed-word printable tool.
Read by scripts/check-printable-tool-duplication.js. An entry stops that gate
billing one pair; it does not hide the pair, which every run still prints.
SAME BAR AS EVERY OTHER LEDGER IN THIS REPO (translation_parity_exceptions.json,
english_parent_exceptions.json, library_hub_exclusions.json): an entry is a
discussed decision between the agent and the owner, never added unilaterally and
never added to make a PR pass. If the gate flags a pair, the default fix is
Hub-vs-Spoke Rule 3 — the page that owns the query keeps the tool, the other keeps
Ships empty on purpose. The site's existing collisions (the seven 'in cursive'
one-word spokes, and the de/pl alphabet-coloring pairs awaiting a locale decision)
are pre-existing at the merge base, so the gate already reports rather than bills
them and they need no entry.
`pages` are routes as the gate prints them: no leading slash, no /index.html.

exceptions.reason: Owner decision 2026-09-22: every locale carries the same two tracing pages English carries, so the name sheet and the letter sheet are separate pages in all seven locales rather than one page doing both. This is the SAME pair English already runs (printables/name-tracing <-> printables/letter-tracing, pre-existing at the merge base and reported by every run), reaching de because the de letter-tracing page now exists. The two pages do not compete for one query: 'Namen nachspuren' and 'Buchstaben nachspuren' are different searches, the pages target them separately, and each links to the other with a one-line pointer (Rule 3 is applied, not skipped). The signature collides only because German uses one word for both sheets -- 'Nachspuren' -- which is a property of the language, not of the pages: it, pl and pt build the identical pair in the same change and do NOT collide, because those languages name the two sheets differently (pregrafismo, slad, pontilhado). Raised with the owner as the open question in the 2026-09-20 printables locale-coverage analysis, section 5, and decided there.
